english_fact_card.why_now: The timetabling issue that caused delays has been resolved, allowing initial highways work to begin on site.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Local residents and commuters can expect a new rail connection in Cheadle, improving access to the network and potentially boosting the area.

english_fact_card.what_happened: Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) agreed a long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) with AGR Power for renewable energy, moving the Bee Network towards becoming the UK's first carbon-neutral public transport system.
english_fact_card.where: Greater Manchester; renewable energy from AGR's solar development in the east of England.
english_fact_card.when: Announced 20 September 2026; agreement for up to 20 years.
english_fact_card.who_affected: TfGM, Bee Network users, and the wider Greater Manchester public.
english_fact_card.why_now: The deal provides energy cost certainty and supports new renewable energy infrastructure, with 42 GWh per year secured, equivalent to Metrolink's current power use.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Shows progress on decarbonising public transport and may influence future energy costs and infrastructure.
english_fact_card.reader_action: No immediate action required; just be aware of the development.

english_fact_card.what_happened: Plans were announced to transform the Grade II-listed Shena Simon Campus on Whitworth Street into a £60m 'lifestyle' hotel, The Oliver, Curio Collection by Hilton.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Local residents, businesses, and visitors; the project is funded and owned by a family office led by Oliver Cookson.
english_fact_card.why_now: The plans were revealed today, marking a major transformation of a historic building formerly part of The Manchester College.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Significant investment and regeneration in the city centre; potential new hospitality and cultural offering.
english_fact_card.reader_action: No immediate action; those interested can follow planning application progress.

content:161be0e31aa3e9ae465e89f64edaaa23.title: Train disruption RECAP as services between London and Manchester cancelled, diverted or delayed
content:161be0e31aa3e9ae465e89f64edaaa23.english_reader_card: Train services between London and Manchester are disrupted due to a safety inspection between Milton Keynes Central and Rugby. Delays of up to 20 minutes, cancellations, and diversions via Northampton are expected until 5pm.

english_fact_card.what_happened: Train services between London and Manchester are cancelled, diverted, or delayed due to a safety inspection of the track between Milton Keynes Central and Rugby.
english_fact_card.where: Between Milton Keynes Central and Rugby, affecting Avanti West Coast services to/from Manchester.
english_fact_card.when: 16 September 2026, disruption expected to last until 5pm.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Passengers travelling between London and Manchester.
english_fact_card.why_now: A safety inspection has led to reduced speeds on some lines, causing delays of up to 20 minutes and some cancellations or diversions via Northampton.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Essential for anyone planning to travel between London and Manchester today.
english_fact_card.reader_action: Check your journey before travelling; allow extra time or consider alternative routes.

content:3ce83b815ac334117e8f995d2173e502.title: The Mancunian Way: Cash cow
content:3ce83b815ac334117e8f995d2173e502.english_reader_card: St John Street in Manchester has generated up to £724,000 in parking fines over three years, with 22,606 penalty charge notices issued. Some drivers claim the signage is confusing, but the council says it is clear.

english_fact_card.what_happened: A Freedom of Information request revealed that St John Street in Manchester has generated up to £724,000 in parking fines over three years, with 22,606 penalty charge notices issued.
english_fact_card.when: Data covers three years since January 2024; reported 16 September 2026.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Motorists parking on St John Street; Manchester City Council.
english_fact_card.why_now: The figures were obtained by ParkAppeal and highlight criticism of the council's parking enforcement, with some drivers claiming signage is confusing.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Reveals the scale of parking fines on a single street and raises questions about signage and enforcement.
english_fact_card.reader_action: No direct action; motorists should be aware of parking restrictions on St John Street.

content:b7d5d2bbed8cb2a88e39b8fe41493765.title: Police storm Manchester Airport plane and arrest passenger after boy left with fractured skull
content:b7d5d2bbed8cb2a88e39b8fe41493765.english_reader_card: Police arrested a man on a Manchester-bound plane at Malaga Airport after a 12-year-old boy was left with a fractured skull in an alleged hit-and-run in the Costa del Sol. The suspect was taken off the flight on Tuesday morning; Torremolinos Town Hall confirmed the arrest but has not released his age or nationality.

english_fact_card.what_happened: Police arrested a man on a Manchester-bound flight at Malaga Airport in connection with an alleged hit-and-run that left a 12-year-old boy with a fractured skull.
english_fact_card.where: Malaga Airport, Spain; incident occurred at a zebra crossing in the Costa del Sol.
english_fact_card.who_affected: The 12-year-old victim, his family, and the suspect.
english_fact_card.why_now: The arrest was made as the suspect attempted to leave Spain on a flight to Manchester.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Highlights a cross-border police operation and the serious consequences of a hit-and-run.
english_fact_card.reader_action: No immediate action required; follow updates from Spanish authorities.

content:9b46aa497f48233a962206a46424f2df.title: Man who downloaded vile images of children given community order
content:9b46aa497f48233a962206a46424f2df.english_reader_card: Stephen Gordon, 37, of Partington, Trafford, was given an 18-month community order and a sexual harm prevention order at Manchester Crown Court for making indecent images of children.

english_fact_card.what_happened: Stephen Gordon, 37, was sentenced to an 18-month community order and a sexual harm prevention order for three offences of making indecent images of children across three categories.
english_fact_card.where: Manchester Crown Court, Crown Square, Manchester. Gordon is from Central Road, Partington, Trafford.
english_fact_card.when: Sentencing took place on September 15, 2026. He pleaded guilty on August 28 and was released on bail.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Stephen Gordon, 37, of Partington, Trafford.
english_fact_card.why_now: The sentencing was reported today, September 17, 2026.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Provides an update on a local court case involving serious offences.
english_fact_card.reader_action: No specific action required.

content:3bbeb7b0c5e3255ab18d65dffc29dd6f.title: Andy Burnham names 20 schools and groups in Greater Manchester given £1.4m boost in 'people power'
content:3bbeb7b0c5e3255ab18d65dffc29dd6f.english_reader_card: Andy Burnham announced that 20 schools and groups in Greater Manchester will share a £1.4 million pot to build their own clean energy projects, part of the government's 'People's Power' initiative.

english_fact_card.what_happened: Andy Burnham announced that 20 schools and groups in Greater Manchester will have access to a £1.4 million pot to build and control their own clean energy supply.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Schools and community groups in Greater Manchester.
english_fact_card.why_now: The government's 'People's Power' project is launching a £30 million fund today to support local clean energy projects.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Highlights funding opportunities for local schools and groups to develop clean energy projects.
english_fact_card.reader_action: Schools and groups may check eligibility for the funding.

content:278a3f663a4d7c6980ad7b9623824767.title: Woman tells jury she did not have sex with man accused of raping her because he 'creeped her out'
content:278a3f663a4d7c6980ad7b9623824767.english_reader_card: In the Rochdale historic sexual abuse trial, a woman known as Girl A told the jury she did not have sex with defendant Arshad Mohammed because he 'creeped her out'.

english_fact_card.what_happened: A woman, known as Girl A, told a jury she did not have sex with Arshad Mohammed, who is accused of raping her as a child, because he 'creeped her out'.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Girl A, Girl B, Girl C, and six men accused of historic sexual offences.
english_fact_card.why_now: The trial is ongoing and this testimony was reported today.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Provides an update on a significant historic sexual abuse trial.
english_fact_card.reader_action: No specific action required.

content:5f46d053da587c6e64a6f05ae680c9fe.title: Warning notice issued for Greater Manchester hospital
content:5f46d053da587c6e64a6f05ae680c9fe.english_reader_card: The CQC issued a warning notice to Wigan's Royal Albert Edward Infirmary after finding excessively long A&E waits, including one patient waiting 44 hours for a bed.

english_fact_card.what_happened: The Care Quality Commission issued a warning notice to the NHS trust running Royal Albert Edward Infirmary in Wigan after inspectors found excessively long waits in the emergency department, including one patient waiting 44 hours for a bed.
english_fact_card.when: Warning notice issued following an inspection; reported on September 17, 2026.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Patients using urgent and emergency services and medical care at the hospital.
english_fact_card.why_now: The CQC inspection report and warning notice were made public today.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Alerts residents to serious delays and quality concerns at a local hospital.
english_fact_card.reader_action: Patients may need to consider alternative services or expect delays.

content:517f7083a2a408dff627c1ae2f401be3.title: 'I've beaten cancer four times thanks to a robot surgeon'
content:517f7083a2a408dff627c1ae2f401be3.english_reader_card: Scott Robinson, 60, from Bramhall, Stockport, has survived cancer four times thanks to a robot surgeon, as told in the MEN's Survivors series.

english_fact_card.what_happened: Scott Robinson, 60, has survived cancer four times, crediting a robot surgeon. His partner Poppy Humphrey, 40, describes his bravery during treatment that 'felt like torture'.
english_fact_card.when: Published 17 September 2026; cancer journey began May 2025 with ear pain
english_fact_card.who_affected: Scott Robinson and his partner Poppy Humphrey
english_fact_card.why_now: Part of the Manchester Evening News' Survivors series, fifteenth instalment, published today.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Inspirational local story of resilience and NHS care.
english_fact_card.reader_action: No direct action; read the full interview for personal account.

content:07b980c5dfbc06735291125d21fa0e09.title: The exciting plans for a new University of Salford business school
content:07b980c5dfbc06735291125d21fa0e09.english_reader_card: University of Salford has unveiled plans for a new Business School at 43-44 The Crescent, with a public consultation now open.

english_fact_card.what_happened: University of Salford has revealed plans for a new Business School building at 43-44 The Crescent, Salford. The multi-million pound project would transform the site into a three-storey block to house courses including Business Management, HR, Supply Chain and Logistics, Digital Business, Law, Marketing, Economics, and Accounting.
english_fact_card.when: Plans revealed on 17 September 2026; consultation ongoing.
english_fact_card.who_affected: University of Salford students and staff, local residents, and the wider Salford community.
english_fact_card.why_now: The university is seeking public opinion on the 'ambitious' plans as part of its campus expansion, funded by development partnership ECF, Salford City Council, and the University of Salford.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Local residents and prospective students can see how the campus will change and have an opportunity to comment on the plans.
english_fact_card.reader_action: View the plans and submit feedback to the university if interested.

content:2305ac58bfebca18a637f4c52cc8c3fd.title: Stockport council begrudgingly signs off plan that will change borough forever after government threats
content:2305ac58bfebca18a637f4c52cc8c3fd.english_reader_card: Stockport Council has reluctantly approved its Local Plan, which will guide development of 24,253 homes across the borough until 2042.

english_fact_card.what_happened: Stockport Council has signed off the latest stage of its Local Plan, which sets out development across the borough until 2042. The plan includes 24,253 new homes and new employment opportunities, with a mix of brownfield and greenbelt development. Council chiefs expressed reluctance but agreed it was necessary to retain control over future development.
english_fact_card.when: Signed off at a town hall meeting on 17 September 2026; plan covers 2026-2042.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Stockport residents, developers, and local businesses.
english_fact_card.why_now: The council was under government orders to produce the plan and faced threats if it did not comply.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Residents can understand the scale of future housing and development in their area and the council's position.
english_fact_card.reader_action: No immediate action required; stay informed about future planning consultations.

content:79a4ff9b3d8420a785b962ef1ea66403.title: United Utility issue update after massive sinkhole appears on Bury Street
content:79a4ff9b3d8420a785b962ef1ea66403.english_reader_card: Heywood Road in Prestwich remains closed after a sinkhole caused by a collapsed sewer; United Utilities engineers are on site.

english_fact_card.what_happened: A massive sinkhole appeared on Heywood Road in Prestwich, Bury, caused by a collapsed sewer. United Utilities engineers have begun repairs, and the road remains closed for the foreseeable future.
english_fact_card.when: Sinkhole appeared on Tuesday 15 September 2026; update issued 16 September 2026.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Motorists, local residents, and bus passengers using Heywood Road.
english_fact_card.why_now: United Utilities has issued an update on the repair work and road closure.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Drivers and commuters need to know the road is closed and plan alternative routes.
english_fact_card.reader_action: Avoid Heywood Road and use alternative routes until further notice.

content:9c5d0811aa40336c19add73139e5f18d.title: Boy under investigation after TikTok knife threats to Salford schools
content:9c5d0811aa40336c19add73139e5f18d.english_reader_card: A boy is under investigation after TikTok knife threats targeting Co-op Academy Walkden in Salford led to bag checks.

english_fact_card.what_happened: A boy is under investigation after an alleged hoax knife threat on TikTok targeting Co-op Academy Walkden in Salford. The posts, which included images of a bladed weapon and armed police, led to bag checks at the school.
english_fact_card.when: Threats circulated on 3 September 2026; investigation ongoing as of 16 September 2026.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Students, parents, and staff at Co-op Academy Walkden.
english_fact_card.why_now: Police are investigating the incident, and the MEN has reported on the investigation.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Parents and the local community can be aware of the incident and the police response.
english_fact_card.reader_action: No specific action required; follow updates from the school or police.

content:856a3166bf97533746e154614b9bf84c.title: "This street is usually quiet, but it's not out of the ordinary for something like this to happen in this area"
content:856a3166bf97533746e154614b9bf84c.english_reader_card: A 16-year-old boy was stabbed on Emmett Street East in Harpurhey, Manchester, on Wednesday afternoon. He was taken to hospital with injuries not considered life-threatening or life-changing; police are investigating.

english_fact_card.what_happened: A 16-year-old boy was stabbed and taken to hospital with injuries not life-threatening or life-changing.
english_fact_card.who_affected: A 16-year-old boy.
english_fact_card.why_now: Police are investigating and a cordon was in place but has now been lifted.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Residents should be aware of the incident and ongoing police investigation.
english_fact_card.reader_action: No specific action required; follow local news for updates.

content:51f6624b444f28770a12f16b6c367100.title: Number 10 North adding 'significant additional demands' on GMP as force battles £10m budget gap
content:51f6624b444f28770a12f16b6c367100.english_reader_card: Greater Manchester Police is facing a predicted £10m budget overspend this year, partly due to demands from the new Number 10 North office in Manchester, deputy mayor Kate Green told a public meeting on Wednesday.

english_fact_card.what_happened: Greater Manchester's deputy mayor Kate Green said the opening of Number 10 North in Manchester has placed significant additional demands on Greater Manchester Police, contributing to a predicted £10m budget overspend.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Greater Manchester Police and local residents.
english_fact_card.why_now: A new report revealed GMP is facing a budget overspend predicted to hit nearly £10m this year.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Explains pressures on local policing and potential impact on services.
english_fact_card.reader_action: No immediate action; follow updates on GMP budget measures.
